title: Counter-Selector Wave 36: portable proof closure and operational remainder
purpose: Adjudicate the post-Wave-35 source advances: recognize one complete same-package portable proof-verification chain, preserve the absence of successor operation and external review, and prevent richer package features or end-user use from being converted into a complete operational handoff.

complete_portable_proof_chain_requires: one portable proof object binds transfer, audit lineage, evidence bundle, policy decision, trusted time, verification certificate, and both participant signatures
the verifier recalculates every bound layer from source artifacts rather than accepting a cached derived root
substitution of audit lineage, bundle manifest, or incoming signature fails closed
the incoming participant signs the same reconstructed proof binding as the outgoing participant
complete_operational_handoff_requires: the verified package also carries operational authority, credentials, dependencies, access, open decisions, deadlines, rollback, and safe-decline state
the recipient acknowledges an inspectable package inventory rather than only a cryptographic root
the successor operates from the verified package without hidden predecessor state
an independent reviewer can inspect the same package, acknowledgment, conflict behavior, and resulting operation

components.versioned_package_identity: PortableHandoverProof binds ProofID, transfer, audit entry, Evidence Bundle, Bundle signature, trusted timestamp, Verification Certificate, and fixed outgoing and incoming signatures
components.exact_integrity_binding: the verifier rechecks Bundle signature, trusted timestamp, certificate, reconstructed binding, and both Participant signatures in canonical order
components.outgoing_and_incoming_identity_or_role: FromParticipantID and ToParticipantID are carried by the transfer and fixed outgoing and incoming signer roles must match those identities
components.authority_and_credential_ledger: TrustStore resolution, key identity, algorithm, validity, revocation, signing time, and nondelegated Participant identity are verified
components.dependency_and_access_inventory: the complete evidentiary proof dependencies are bound; operational credentials, physical access, and successor-runtime dependencies are outside the package
components.open_decision_and_deadline_inventory: the completed Policy decision is replayed and certified; operational open decisions, deadlines, and exception queues are not represented
components.rollback_safe_decline_and_conflict_handl: audit, Bundle, certificate, role, key, time, and signature mismatches fail closed; physical rollback and successor safe-decline behavior are outside scope
components.recipient_acceptance_of_the_same_bound_o: the incoming Participant signs the same reconstructed complete proof binding, but does not acknowledge a human-readable package inventory
components.successor_operation_from_package_state: not observed; the merged PR explicitly keeps physical actuation outside PDS scope
components.independent_verification: every bound layer is recalculated from source artifacts inside one repository implementation; no external institution or human reviewer adjudicates the result

positive_findings: One merged verifier starts from the complete portable proof rather than a cached binding.
The same object binds responsibility transfer, audit lineage, Bundle integrity, Policy replay, trusted time, certificate, and both Participant signatures.
Incoming and outgoing Participant identities sign the same reconstructed proof root.
Independent-layer substitution fails closed for audit lineage, Bundle manifest, and incoming signature.
The hosted repository verification run passed on the merged head.
known_limits: The incoming signature is cryptographic acceptance of a binding, not an itemized recipient package receipt.
Operational credentials, dependencies, open decisions, deadlines, and rollback state are not part of the proof.
No successor operation or physical actuation from the verified package is observed.
The verifier is same-system independent recalculation, not external institutional review.
A complete portable proof is not a person-level custody or complete-operator finding.

components.versioned_package_identity: ARSAS-IOFAT-PACKAGE-1.0 evolves into a user-facing .arsas project containing snapshot, workbook, evidence, native PDF, native XLSX, and README
components.exact_integrity_binding: snapshot, workbook, evidence journals, PDF, and XLSX hashes are represented; modern report metadata can still be omitted through legacy fallback
components.outgoing_and_incoming_identity_or_role: exporter and importer software roles exist; no named outgoing and incoming participants bind one package
components.authority_and_credential_ledger: active-session export is blocked, but environment authority, credentials, and access are not inventoried
components.dependency_and_access_inventory: application, workbook, evidence, and report dependencies are partly represented; aggregate archive expansion and environment dependencies remain incomplete
components.open_decision_and_deadline_inventory: test-point state is preserved; no package-level inventory of open engineering decisions, deadlines, and owners is acknowledged
components.rollback_safe_decline_and_conflict_handl: atomic writes, tamper rejection, collision preservation, and continuity downgrade exist, but seven unresolved safety and fidelity findings remain
components.recipient_acceptance_of_the_same_bound_o: automated import succeeds; no named recipient acknowledges an exact package digest and inventory
components.successor_operation_from_package_state: automated cross-root restoration and report generation are tested; independently observed field operation is absent
components.independent_verification: two external automated review surfaces expose seven unresolved findings; no package clearance or external institutional review exists

positive_findings: A real portable project implementation survives export and import across distinct workspace roots.
The second generation adds native PDF and XLSX result artifacts with manifest hashes.
Tampered snapshot and native report bytes are rejected in regression tests.
Continuity loss downgrades partial ON evidence instead of silently claiming completion.
External automated review remains visible and identifies concrete failure modes.
known_limits: Evidence journals from different workbook hashes can mix under the same ProjectId.
Import can overwrite newer local progress with an older package snapshot.
Per-entry limits do not establish an aggregate uncompressed archive budget.
Missing required manifest strings can escape the documented import-failure path.
Modern report hash metadata can be omitted and misclassified as legacy.
Non-ASCII evidence text is silently altered or erased in the native PDF.
Per-IED summary headers omit FAIL counts and can conceal category totals.

components.versioned_package_identity: absent; repository documentation and a live deployment are referenced without one operational package identity or digest
components.exact_integrity_binding: absent for the customer transition object
components.outgoing_and_incoming_identity_or_role: team and customer roles are observable, but not cryptographically or package-bound
components.authority_and_credential_ledger: the document mentions environment variables and hosting costs, but no complete authority or credential transfer receipt exists
components.dependency_and_access_inventory: source repository, server, model weights, OpenRouter key, and hosting dependencies are described incompletely
components.open_decision_and_deadline_inventory: known limitations and optional follow-ups are named, but not bound to a versioned package with owners and rollback state
components.rollback_safe_decline_and_conflict_handl: not established for the transition package
components.recipient_acceptance_of_the_same_bound_o: the customer accepts and uses the product, not an identified package inventory

positive_findings: A real recipient independently operated the product rather than merely acknowledging a role.
Two sequential uploads produced updated result and chart state.
The recipient used written guidance without live step-by-step direction.
Known limitations and follow-up items remained visible rather than being erased by the successful demonstration.
known_limits: No single versioned operational package or package digest is identified.
No package-level recipient inventory receipt exists.
Credentials, authority, dependencies, open decisions, and rollback state are incomplete.
The team remains available afterward, so hidden predecessor dependence is not excluded.
End-user product use does not establish maintainership or operational ownership transfer.

next_action: Acquire one same-object transition that joins the Cargo-grade complete portable proof chain to an inspectable package inventory receipt and observed successor operation without hidden predecessor state. Continue ARSAS only after all seven review findings are resolved and receipted. Do not assemble Cargo proof, ARSAS execution, and BasketForm field use into one handoff.
